Stated Claim / Post Context:
Husband arrested in wife's disappearance after family kept getting mystery texts

Epifanio Gaminde allegedly mailed his missing wife's credit cards to a relative in the Philippines to create the illusion she was alive overseas.

Actual Article Body:

Volusia County Sheriff Mike Chitwood details the investigation that led to a first-degree murder charge against Epifanio Gaminde in the disappearance of his wife, Maria. (Volusia Sheriff's Office via Facebook)

A Florida man accused of murdering his missing wife allegedly sent her identification and credit cards to a relative in the Philippines as part of an elaborate effort to make it appear she was alive and living overseas, authorities said.

Epifanio IX Ramos Gaminde was indicted on a first-degree murder charge in the disappearance of his wife, Maria Gaminde, whose family has had no confirmed contact with her since January 2024.

Her body has not been found, but investigators searched the couple's DeBary, Florida, property Tuesday after a neighbor reported seeing Gaminde doing extensive work behind the home around the time his wife disappeared.

CALIFORNIA NURSE'S HUSBAND CLAIMED ICE TOOK HER — NOW HE'S CHARGED WITH MURDER

Maria's family reported her missing in January 2024 after losing contact with her. By July of that year, relatives were raising concerns with investigators about text messages, emails and credit-card activity that purportedly came from Maria overseas.

Epifanio IX Ramos Gaminde was indicted on a first-degree murder charge in the disappearance of his wife, Maria Gaminde. (Volusia County Sheriff's Office)

"The family starts to contact us and say, 'Hey, something's not right. These text messages and emails that we're getting, the spending on her credit cards, too. Something's not right,'" Volusia County Sheriff Mike Chitwood said during a news conference Tuesday.

SISTER OF MISSING DC MOM SPEAKS OUT AFTER EX’S ARREST EXPOSES 'HORRIFYING' ABUSIVE RELATIONSHIP

Gaminde told investigators the couple was having marital problems and claimed his wife had left for either the Philippines or Japan.

Detectives examined digital and forensic evidence and interviewed neighbors as the investigation increasingly focused on Gaminde. Investigators also learned he had previously been arrested twice for domestic violence, Chitwood said.

Maria Gaminde’s family reported her missing in 2024 after losing contact with her and later questioning messages and financial activity purportedly coming from her overseas. (Volusia County Sheriff's Office)

NAVY RESERVIST ACCUSED OF MURDERING WIFE AND HIDING HER BODY IN FREEZER ARRESTED AFTER INTERNATIONAL MANHUNT

The investigation eventually stretched overseas, with the FBI helping Volusia County investigators and prosecutors navigate international legal issues before a detective and prosecutor traveled to the Philippines to interview Gaminde's niece.

An investigator examines an area behind the Gamindes’ DeBary home during a search of the property. Maria Gaminde’s body has not been recovered. (Volusia County Sheriff's Office)

"She gives up everything," Chitwood said. "She even gives us more information that the FBI has to work with international partners to recover digital evidence from when it occurred."

6 IN 10 IDENTITY CRIMES NOW BEGIN WITH A NEW ACCOUNT

Gaminde allegedly emailed his niece Maria's important documents, including her driver's license and credit cards, and instructed her what to do with them, the sheriff said. Investigators believe the activity was intended to create the appearance that Maria was alive and avoiding contact with her family, friends and law enforcement.

Authorities traced Maria's last known activity to December 2023. Investigators determined Maria and her children visited Disney World's Magic Kingdom on Dec. 16 after confirming their fingerprints were used to enter the park.

Volusia County investigators search the DeBary, Florida, property where Maria Gaminde lived with her husband, who is now charged with her murder. (Volusia County Sheriff's Office)

ACCUSED WIFE KILLER BARRY MORPHEW BACK BEHIND BARS AFTER SEPARATE INCIDENT THAT SKYROCKETED BOND: PROSECUTORS

Four days later, Gaminde allegedly sent his wife a text asking where she was. Communications from Maria then stopped before messages purportedly from her began coming from overseas.

Despite those communications and the apparent activity on Maria's accounts, investigators found no evidence that she was still alive.

TEXAS MAN ACCUSED OF KILLING PREGNANT WIFE ALLEGEDLY CUTS OFF ANKLE MONITOR AND FLEES TO ITALY

"There's no financial trail. There's nothing that would indicate that Maria is alive," Chitwood said.

During Tuesday's search of the couple's property, investigators focused on an area behind the home where concrete appeared to have been added. Chitwood cautioned that investigators did not know whether the search would lead them to Maria's remains.

PARENTS FOUND BURIED BEHIND HOME IN WEALTHY NEIGHBORHOOD AS POLICE LAUNCH INTERNATIONAL MANHUNT FOR SON

Epifanio IX Ramos Gaminde is detained in body-camera footage. Authorities say he was already in custody when a grand jury indicted him for his wife’s murder. (Volusia County Sheriff's Office)

FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X

"We may get lucky, we may not get lucky," Chitwood said.

Prosecutors said they are prepared to pursue the first-degree murder case even if Maria's body is never recovered.

PROSECUTORS SEEKING DEATH PENALTY FOR DEPORTED ILLEGAL ALIEN INDICTED IN MURDER OF SISTER-IN-LAW

R.J. Larizza, state attorney for Florida's 7th Judicial Circuit, said the outcome of Tuesday's search would not change the state's plans to prosecute Gaminde.

Investigators search the property where Maria Gaminde lived in DeBary, Florida, after her husband was indicted on a first-degree murder charge in her disappearance. (Volusia County Sheriff's Office)

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

"We're fully prepared to move forward without the body," Larizza said. "And I have complete and total confidence in our ability to prosecute this case."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FROM THE FOX TRUE CRIME HUB

Gaminde was already in custody after being stopped for allegedly driving without a license when the grand jury returned the murder indictment. He is being held without bond at the Volusia County Branch Jail and also faces an immigration detainer from U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement.

SEND US A TIP

Gaminde and Maria came to the United States together around 2008 and have three young sons, the sheriff said. The children were with their father when he was taken into custody and have since been reunited with Maria's family.

Epifanio IX Ramos Gaminde is seen in body-camera footage before his arrest. He was later indicted on a first-degree murder charge in his wife’s disappearance. (Volusia County Sheriff's Office)

GOT A TIP?

Chitwood said the children had been denied contact with their mother's side of the family.

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

Gaminde has been interviewed repeatedly during the investigation, but authorities do not believe the accounts he provided.

GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL

"Every interview he has given us has just been a lie," Chitwood said.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

The investigation remains ongoing.
